unexpected_findings.title: Certified-run JSON misdescribes reference generation
unexpected_findings.expected: Measurement provenance describes the reference actually used.
unexpected_findings.observed: All three current report.json files say measurement.reference='independent Battle legal-action enumeration in separate process'. The requested --reference-file is a pre-generated complete finite-target-assignment certificate; its method states 'complete finite target assignments; all feasible last hitters; pre/post evolution; exact injective dominance'.
unexpected_findings.impact: A reader of machine-readable measurement metadata can wrongly infer reference full legal-action enumeration was performed in a separate process for this run. Numerical completeness/equality/replay and required Markdown fields passed.

evidence: F1 PASS: delivered fixture has three distinct nonuniform 5v5 boards including varied-5v5. Docs and suite catalog identify target assignment/evolution in varied; cooperative lethal and sacrifice/tradeoffs in allocation; spent/sick/injured/super-finisher timing in timing-finisher. Fixtures contain no ability/card actions; every returned action type is attack, evolve or super_evolve.

F2 PASS: certificate complete=true/status=PASS for all 3; method/independence/finished assignment and endpoint counts present. Independent executor compared every bench.signature(candidate) to entire certificate expected set in both directions, using only documented normalization. All product complete=true, missing=extra=0.

F3 PASS: inspected all saved replay_answers and corresponding witness candidates from current execution artifacts. Indices exactly cover every candidate once; each actual replay signature equals that candidate signature; reported replay_coverage=all, no errors. This uses the fixed-spec artifact observation option, not new HTTP replay calls.

F4 PASS: report.json and directly read report.md identify case, correctness PASS, product completion 1/1, certified-reference completion, reference.json and all-answer links, finite nonnegative analysis ms and positive peak memory. Markdown states time=analysis only and memory=process peak through analysis including Python/input/cache; units ms/MiB; JSON bytes and Windows PeakWorkingSetSize.
F5 PASS: all executions normal exit 0, complete=true with fully complete references; no truncation, timeout, or unverified run labeled as a complete match. Markdown explicitly explains UNVERIFIED.

UX1 PASS: default and delivered-suite --list-cases each executed once. IDs and commands discovered through docs/combat-benchmark.md; source reads 0. Exact commands/logs in execution.json and *.stdout.txt.

UX2 PASS: each generated Markdown independently contains correctness, completion, analysis ms, peak MiB, measurement scope and linked complete reference and answers. No mandatory metric required JSON to discover.
UX3 PASS: external time.monotonic around process launch through normal exit; per-case wall 40.078, 46.375, 3.234 seconds, each below fixed 60 seconds. Each selected case run exactly once; no retries.
UX4 N/A: CLI machine-use journey; clicks/focus/viewport/scroll/manual surface transitions not applicable.

Budget: 12-minute journey cap; commands used 94.203 seconds including two catalog invocations; artifact inspection/report performed within cap. T1 single executor; T2 independent parallel executor managed by parent.

cleanup.evidence: All five directly created CLI processes observed exited with code 0; no timeout/kill needed. Own harness exited. Artifacts preserved at C:\Users\tasog\source\shadowverse-deckmaker\output\combat-hard-acceptance-cli. No server or other process touched.

blind_spots: T1 partial report only; merge T2 from its independent executor before full-spec report lint can succeed.
Reference exhaustive construction was reviewed via method and completion certificate; expensive independent reference generation was not repeated, as allowed by fixed spec.
Replay legality observed through permitted current-run saved replay artifacts, not independently reissued HTTP requests.
